gdl-01-c1.text: Michael M. Bronstein, Joan Bruna, Taco Cohen, Petar Veličković (2021). Geometric Deep Learning: Grids, Groups, Graphs, Geodesics, and Gauges. arXiv (arXiv:2104.13478).
gdl-01-c1.quote: provides a common mathematical framework to study the most successful neural network architectures
gdl-01-c1.claim: In 2021, Michael Bronstein, Joan Bruna, Taco Cohen, and Petar Veličković published the monograph Geometric Deep Learning: Grids, Groups, Graphs, Geodesics, and Gauges.

gdl-01-c3.text: Taco Cohen, Max Welling (2016). Group Equivariant Convolutional Networks. Proceedings of the 33rd International Conference on Machine Learning (PMLR 48:2990-2999).
gdl-01-c3.quote: a natural generalization of convolutional neural networks that reduces sample complexity by exploiting symmetries
gdl-01-c3.claim: group-equivariant CNNs (G-CNNs), introduced by Cohen and Welling in 2016

gdl-06-c2.text: John Jumper et al (2021). Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold. Nature.
gdl-06-c2.quote: d, Structure module including Invariant point attention (IPA) module.
gdl-06-c2.claim: The structure module of AlphaFold introduces Invariant Point Attention (IPA), which carries the network's geometry.

gdl-04-c2.text: Keyulu Xu, Weihua Hu, Jure Leskovec, Stefanie Jegelka (2018). How Powerful are Graph Neural Networks?. arXiv.
gdl-04-c2.quote: as powerful as the Weisfeiler-Lehman graph isomorphism test
gdl-04-c2.claim: The same paper introduced GIN (Graph Isomorphism Network), which uses sum aggregation plus an MLP and matches the 1-WL bound exactly.

gdl-04-c3.text: Qimai Li, Zhichao Han, Xiao-Ming Wu (2018). Deeper Insights into Graph Convolutional Networks for Semi-Supervised Learning. arXiv.
gdl-04-c3.quote: First, we show that the graph convolution of the GCN model is actually a special form of Laplacian smoothing
gdl-04-c3.claim: Li, Han, and Wu (2018) formalized this connection between GCNs and Laplacian smoothing.

gdl-04-c3.text: Jake Topping, Francesco Di Giovanni, Benjamin Paul Chamberlain, Xiaowen Dong, Michael M. Bronstein (2021). Understanding over-squashing and bottlenecks on graphs via curvature. arXiv (ICLR 2022).
gdl-04-c3.quote: prove that negatively curved edges are responsible for the over-squashing issue.
gdl-04-c3.claim: Topping, Di Giovanni, Chamberlain, Dong, and Bronstein (2022) connected oversquashing to negative Ricci curvature on the graph

gdl-04-c1.text: Justin Gilmer, Samuel S. Schoenholz, Patrick F. Riley, Oriol Vinyals, George E. Dahl (2017). Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry. arXiv.
gdl-04-c1.quote: we reformulate existing models into a single common framework we call Message Passing Neural Networks
gdl-04-c1.claim: Almost every graph neural network can be cast as a message passing layer (Gilmer, Schoenholz, Riley, Vinyals, Dahl, 2017).

gdl-03-c2.text: Taco S. Cohen, Mario Geiger, Jonas Köhler, Max Welling (2018). Spherical CNNs. arXiv (ICLR 2018).
gdl-03-c2.quote: The spherical correlation satisfies a generalized Fourier theorem, which allows us to compute it efficiently
gdl-03-c2.claim: Cohen, Geiger, Köhler, and Welling's 2018 Spherical CNNs used Fourier analysis on SO(3)

gdl-05-c1.text: Victor Garcia Satorras, Emiel Hoogeboom, Max Welling (2021). E(n) Equivariant Graph Neural Networks. arXiv.
gdl-05-c1.quote: our work does not require computationally expensive higher-order representations in intermediate layers while it still achieves competitive or better performance.
gdl-05-c1.claim: EGNN (Satorras, Hoogeboom, Welling, 2021) takes a much simpler route
